data.description:
## Prevention remediation for incident 1c0d (operational/architecture lane)

Post-mortem: `9097-2741-6462-424c`. Defense-in-depth against the *trigger* (not the failure mode): many agent sessions ran frontier/opus `review-plan` concurrently on ONE shared Bedrock account, self-inflicting account-level throttling.

### Candidate
A client-side concurrency limiter / rate-limit / shared budget on frontier gate ops so many-agent fan-out cannot drive the shared account into throttling.

### Open decision (ARCHITECTURE — escalate, likely ADR)
This is a design decision, not a mechanical fix. Needs a go/no-go on: whether to add a shared-account budget at all (the 1c0d fix already makes throttling degrade gracefully to retryable, so this is defense-in-depth, not correctness); where the limiter lives (per-host, per-account, MCP-server-mediated); and how it interacts with the existing retry/backoff. Likely warrants an ADR. Do NOT implement until the go/no-go + design are recorded.

### Note
Distinct from the other three prevention tickets: those add **detection** (would have caught the latent defect); this reduces the **trigger frequency**. Lower priority now that throttling degrades to retryable.

### Acceptance criteria (pending decision)
- [ ] Go/no-go recorded; if go, ADR drafted (limiter scope, placement, interaction with retry/backoff).
data.title: Prevention (operational): concurrency budget / rate-limit for shared-account frontier gate ops
